source.title: Fast and Accurate Probing of In-Training LLMs' Downstream Performances
source.authors: Zhicheng Liu; Tianle Lun; Zhi-Bin Wen; Hao-Cong An; Yu-Lin Ou; Jian-Hui Xu; Hao Zhang; Wen-Yi Fang; Yang Zheng; Yangyifan Xu

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether loss predicts downstream task correctness and reports that the loss-fit baseline is near chance overall; it does not test the scaling-law measurements in the claim.
record.gate_note: The loss-fit baseline regresses per-prompt model loss to empirical correctness probability, so its reported outcomes bear on V6. The proposed probes and their results predict correctness from hidden representations, not from scale or pretraining loss, and are not rows for the claim. The paper does not sweep parameters, tokens, or compute, compare power-law fits, or test architecture-shape effects.
record.test_reason: This study builds hidden-state probes that predict per-prompt correctness for OLMo-3-7B checkpoints. Its 'Loss fit' rows are a baseline: an OLS regression from per-prompt loss to per-prompt pass@1, fit within a single checkpoint (800k). V6 is about downstream performance tracking model scale or aggregate pretraining loss across runs or checkpoints. Ranking prompts by their own loss inside one model is a different construct. The study varies no scale, fits no scaling law, and reports no aggregate loss-vs-performance relation across checkpoints. It mentions scaling laws and the limits of perplexity only in the introduction. So it does not test any version, and the loss-fit finding goes under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, with two corrections. The main conclusion is that the Submodel probe predicts per-prompt correctness well (average AUROC 0.789) and transfers from earlier to later checkpoints with a large speedup. The loss-fit result (average AUROC 0.5795) is a baseline comparison. The authors link it to 'emergence', saying training loss does not track complex reasoning ability; they do not test that link.
record.recipe_differences: The study fits ordinary least squares from per-prompt loss to correctness probability; it does not fit scaling laws over model parameters, tokens, or compute.
record.method_sensitivity: Loss-fit AUROC differs by dataset, ranging from 0.4588 on MMLU to 0.7048 on HumanEval.

fits_no_version.finding: On the OLMo-3-7B 800k checkpoint, an OLS fit from per-prompt loss to per-prompt pass@1 ranks prompts near chance. Average AUROC is 0.5795 (range 0.4588 on MMLU to 0.7048 on HumanEval).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within a single checkpoint, a prompt's loss weakly predicts whether the model answers that prompt correctly.

record.problems: The loss-fit assessment is reported for one 7B pretraining checkpoint and per-prompt loss rather than aggregate held-out loss across runs; uncertainty estimates are not reported. The evidence therefore does not establish how loss predicts downstream performance across scale.

untested.parts: All: no loss-vs-parameters, tokens or compute curves.
All: no extrapolation of fitted laws.
All: no shape comparison at fixed parameter count.
All: no other modalities or training regimes.
Aggregate downstream performance as a function of scale or aggregate pretraining loss across runs or checkpoints. The study reports neither.
All: no exponent or fitting-choice comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's labels on V6 are dropped. The loss-fit is an instance-level baseline within one checkpoint, not a scale or aggregate-loss relation, so it cannot support or challenge V6. The cross-checkpoint tables report probe AUROC only; there is no aggregate accuracy-vs-step or loss-vs-step data.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out cross-entropy scaling against parameters, tokens, and compute, including the non-bottleneck conditions and several orders of magnitude.
Prediction of larger-run losses from power laws fit to smaller runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocations and their trends with compute.
Effects of depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
Power-law behavior in other modalities or training regimes.

The study uses per-prompt loss to predict correctness at one pretraining checkpoint; it does not test whether aggregate pretraining loss or model scale predicts downstream performance across runs or checkpoints.
Dependence of scaling-law exponents or compute-optimal allocations on setup and fitting choices, or bending of scaling curves.

rows.subject: OLMo-3-Base-800k checkpoint
rows.operation_detail: Fit ordinary least squares from per-prompt loss to empirical correctness probability; report AUROC.
rows.measure: AUROC for loss-fit prediction of correctness
rows.note: The study identifies AUROC = 0.5 as random guessing.
rows.check: This is a baseline comparator to the study's own probe: per-prompt loss regressed on per-prompt correctness within one checkpoint. It is not downstream performance versus scale or aggregate pretraining loss. An AUROC of 0.4588 is near chance; calling it 'reversed' overreads it.
